gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: She ___ admitted that she had made a mistake (HONEST).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ly forms adverbs: honestly modifies the verb 'admitted'.

gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: The medicine is available without a ___ (PRESCRIBE).
Heavy snow made the mountain road ___ (PASS).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: impossible to travel through (im- + -able)
gaps.explanation: Heavy snow blocks the road, so the negative adjective 'impassable' (im- + pass + -able) is needed.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ until Thursday (SCHEDULE).
gaps.hint: arranged for a new time (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again/afresh: rescheduled means given a new time. The passive needs the past participle.

gaps.sentence: The tracks become ___ after heavy rain (ACCESS).
gaps.explanation: Heavy rain blocks the tracks, so the negative adjective 'inaccessible' (in- + accessible) is needed.
